motion: Locked-off wide, a barely perceptible push-in toward the lit wall. A fine mist falls through the spotlight cone and glitters as it drifts down. The broken-white pool of light on the wall slowly breathes, its off-white shifting between bone, ivory and a faint lilac, like wet paint drying: a colour that doesn't exist. The woman and the man stand still at opposite ends, facing each other; only breath, a drip from her hem, the silk stirring. Neither steps closer. Faces unchanged, no talking, no new people, nothing appears on the wall.
keep_still: Both figures planted at opposite ends of the wall, with no step toward each other. Faces, wet clothes and the bare wall stay as they are. No lip movement.
risk: The scenario describes 1a as an empty wall, but the approved frame has both of them in it. Kling may walk them toward each other, or turn the mist into heavy rain. The wall's colour shift may read as flicker if it is too fast. The timing covers both cards: 'Blanc cassé … Broken white.' and the contract line (109 characters).

motion: Locked-off macro, no camera move. The body stays: both are still, and the gap between his face and her ear never closes; he does not touch her. Only his breath moves: the fine hairs at her nape and the loose strands by her ear stir with each slow exhale, and the tweed weave and lilac collar answer with the faintest lift. A faint warm heat-haze shimmers in the gap between them while the cool blue rim light slides slowly across her black hair. His lips stay parted and still, no speech, no kiss. Faces unchanged, no new people.
keep_still: His face stays at its distance from her ear, with no contact and no kiss on her neck. His lips stay parted but do not move. Her head, bun and jacket do not move.
risk: His parted lips may start mouthing words, or he may lean in to her neck. Reject any take where the gap closes ('He does not touch her', #097). Skin texture on her neck may smear in the macro.

motion: Slow push-in on her profile. Eyes stay closed. She leans the last centimetre, presses her lips softly to the frosted pane and holds; the clear oval around her mouth melts wider, beads of meltwater running down the glass; she eases back a breath's width and her exhale clouds the oval white again as frost creeps back. Outside, the blue-white streetlight blooms and softens like wet paint behind the frost. The face in the glass is only her own reflection and moves with her. No speaking, no other person, hair and jacket still, face unchanged.
keep_still: Her eyes stay closed and her face does not change. Hair, jacket and tie stay still. The reflection stays her own and adds no second face. No speaking: the LITPROM voice is off-face.
risk: The reflection may turn into a second person, which would make the moment read as a kiss with someone. The frost may not re-cloud, and the lips may move as if speaking. The voice draft (80 characters) sets the length, so a 5 s clip at 1.2 gives only 6 s and the shot needs the 10 s clip.

motion: Generate the leaf FALLING (the edit plays it reversed so it rises): the single burnt leaf drifts slowly downward in a gentle spiral, turning on its stem, its veins glowing and dimming like embers as it turns through the light, lit as if through a plane window. The camera tilts down gently with it so it stays near frame centre. Storm clouds roll slowly; the city lights below twinkle softly; a breath of mist. One leaf only: no flames, no sparks, no second leaf, no birds, nothing new in the sky.
keep_still: The leaf keeps its shape and colour: it does not crumble, burn or multiply. The city skyline stays fixed and nothing new appears in the sky.
risk: This follows the scenario's production note: generate the leaf falling, then reverse it. Clouds and mist also play backwards, which is invisible at this speed. The leaf may tumble too fast, or Kling may set it on fire. There are no words, so the shot runs the minimum 4 s, under the three ukulele notes.

motion: Overhead, locked-off, a very slow push-in toward her eyes. First 6 s: she floats near-still on the black sea, gaze into the lens, unblinking; only the water moves: slow swell, rings around her shoulders, wet curls fanning and drifting, the moon path above her breaking into silver brushstrokes. Then, without freezing, she tips her head back and slips under in one smooth motion; black water closes over her face with a real splash, hair last to vanish, rings spreading. The slip stays on. Face unchanged until it goes under, no talking, no one else.
keep_still: Her face and gaze hold until she submerges, and the black satin slip stays fully on. Her body stays near-still for the first 6 s. No lip movement and no second swimmer.
risk: This is the riskiest motion in the batch. Kling may start the plunge early, distort her face as it goes under, or shift the slip. The edit cuts the float, which carries 'stormy — one / two', to the 1.2 s RGB-eye glitch (not counted in 8.5 s), then to the plunge, which carries 'the bait broke off…'. Fallback: render the plunge as its own 5 s clip from k06. If the 1.2 slow-down makes the splash limp, run the plunge part at 1.0.

motion: Behind her, locked-off, at water level. The body stays: she rises only a few centimetres out of the black water, water streaming off her shoulder blade in thin bright rivulets, droplets beading; one slow breath lifts her back. Exactly three wet white feathers stay clinging to her shoulder blade: never four, none falls. Wet curls drip and sway. The moonlit sea ripples in silver brushstrokes. She does not turn; we see only her back and shoulder. Hair colour and skin unchanged, no one else.
keep_still: Exactly three feathers stay fixed on her shoulder blade (Law 3). She stays turned away, showing only her back and shoulder. Hair colour and skin do not change.
risk: The feather count may drift, with a fourth appearing or one falling, which breaks 'three, never four'. A rise that goes too far, or a turn toward camera, crosses the nudity line, so reject either. Her hair reads browner here than blue-black. The frame is approved, so the motion must not shift it either way. The voice is #036 lines 1-2 (62 characters).

motion: Low ground-level camera, a very slow slide toward the scales. Surf foam runs up the black sand and draws back, its thin silver edge stopping short of the scales. Moonlight shimmers on the sea; the scales glint, their mother-of-pearl colour shifting slowly from pearl to lilac to ice-blue as the light travels across them, like an Impressionist sea. The water in the footprint trembles and holds the moon. Palm fronds sway. The scales lie still: they do not crawl or slide. No person, no new footprints, no animals.
keep_still: The scales stay put: they do not crawl, wash away or turn into fish. The footprint keeps its shape. The moon stays fixed. No person.
risk: Kling may animate the scales as creatures, which breaks the impressionism rule, or let the surf wash them away. The #036 voice is split across the two frames: lines 1-2 over 7m (feathers), lines 3-4 ('For nothing you've shed your scales again…', 86 characters) over this frame. That assumes 7m plays first, as the scenario cuts ('She rises… Cut: silver scales').

motion: Very slow push-in on her profile. The body stays: she draws one slow, deep breath through the nose, scent before light; nostrils and throat move, lids stay half-lowered, lips still, no speaking. Behind her, steam rises off the black sand and drifts across the jungle, catching a faint warm frangipani-pink and honey tint, as if the scent were visible. Water drops run slowly down her cheek and jaw; wet curls stir. Distant surf. No flower appears in her hair or anywhere, no one else on the beach, face unchanged.
keep_still: Her face, head and parted lips stay still: one breath, no speaking. No plumeria, because it was removed from the approved frame. No figures on the beach.
risk: The scenario text mentions a plumeria, so Kling may add it back from the prompt or by inference. The approved k09 has no flower. The steam tint must stay subtle or it reads as smoke or CGI. The parted lips may mouth words.

motion: Locked-off. The body stays, the light moves: one thick honey-gold stripe from the shutters sweeps very slowly across her bare shoulder toward the shoulder blade, warming the skin as it passes, its edge soft and liquid like a brushstroke of honey; dust motes turn gold in the beam; a shutter swings gently outside and the slat shadows drift. She lies still, eyes half-open, one slow breath, at most one slow blink. The sheet stays exactly where it is. The faint forehead scar stays pale. No speaking, no one else, face unchanged.
keep_still: Her body lies face-down without rolling or lifting. The sheet does not move at all, per the refusal-safe framing. Her face does not change, and the forehead scar stays a pale hairline, never red.
risk: Kling tends to move the sheet or roll a sleeping figure. Reject any take where the sheet shifts, because 10a/10b are light-only by design. The warm light may redden the scar. The #078 card is 154 characters (11.9 s), so the shot is capped at 10 s and the card may need a split or a slightly faster read.

motion: Locked-off. The honey stripe of light slides slowly onto her shoulder blade and settles; the fine hairs on her skin light up gold and lift slightly, skin answering the air; one slow breath lifts and lowers her back. Eyes stay closed, lips parted and still. The sheet stays exactly where it is; nothing is pulled away and she stays face-down as framed. The light's edge is soft and liquid, like a brushstroke of honey. The faint forehead scar stays pale. No one else, face unchanged.
keep_still: The sheet does not move: nothing is pulled away and she stays face-down as framed. Her eyes stay closed and her lips do not move. The scar stays pale.
risk: The card says 'She pulls the sheet away', but the motion must not. The text carries the action and the light carries the motion. Kling may read 'sheet' and animate a pull. Any take where the sheet slides crosses the refusal line and is rejected, not re-routed.

motion: Locked-off, a barely perceptible push-in toward the mirror. The woman in the room, back to us, does not move at all, her hand stays where it is. Only her reflection moves, slowly: its fingers draw one thin strap off the edge of the shoulder onto the upper arm, while the other hand stays pressed to the chest, holding the black silk fully in place; the bodice never drops. In the mirror it is daylight and palm leaves sway in a warm breeze; the room stays red-lamp night, lamp flames flickering. No lip movement, no speech, faces unchanged, no third woman.
keep_still: The real Kira stays completely still, back to camera, hand at her strap. The reflection's bodice stays up, held at the chest, and the strap goes only to the shoulder edge. No lip movement on either face.
risk: This is the highest consistency and refusal risk. Mirror physics may make Kling move both women or neither. The strap move may overshoot until the bodice drops, so reject anything below the shoulder line (Law 7). Fallback: animate only the mirror region and composite it over a still foreground. The #019 voice is 157 characters (12 s), so the shot is capped at 10 s.

motion: Locked-off at Kira's shoulder. Mila and Jean-Marc walk slowly toward camera along the jetty, two or three unhurried steps; his flat palm stays on her waist, his eyes ahead; her knit dress sways at the slit. Kira, soft in the foreground, stays still, only her curls lifting in the wind. Behind the sharp people, the copper-rose sky and sea smear and shimmer like wet, unblended oil strokes in heat haze; the distant rain curtain drifts. The seaplane stays moored. Faces unchanged, smiles do not grow, no talking, no new people, no statue.
keep_still: Kira stays still in the foreground, back to us. His palm stays on Mila's waist. Faces and expressions do not change: no wider grin, no talking. The seaplane does not move, and no statue or added figure appears.
risk: Walking in a 5 s clip tends to hurry, and the 1.2 slow-down helps. The oil-stroke shimmer may spread onto the people. If it does, reject the take and use the redesign's fallback: a photographic plate with brushstrokes added in post. Jean-Marc's grin may widen. The 5 s clip at 1.2 gives 6 s against a 5.5 s edit, so there is little trim room.

motion: Very slow push-in on Kira. She is near-still, gaze held, at most one slow blink; the narrow band of cool white-gold dawn light stays across her eyes and softly brightens, though nothing casts it, while the copper sunset warms the rest of her face. Behind, in soft focus, Jean-Marc's ringed fingers slowly close tighter on Mila's wrist above the gold bangle; Mila keeps her poised smile and stays still. The water glitters copper. The seaplane stays still. Faces unchanged, no talking, no new people, no added objects.
keep_still: Kira's face, gaze and lips stay still, and the dawn light band stays over her eyes. Mila stays still in her pose. The background faces do not change. The seaplane does not move.
risk: The dawn band may slide off her eyes or harden into an ordinary shadow line. The soft-focus faces behind her may morph. The edit time covers both cards: 'Kira stands slightly behind, watching.' and 'Knows this pain by name…' (98 characters, 7.5 s), so the shot runs longer than the sequence plan's 6 s.

motion: She walks slowly and steadily toward the camera between the tables, unhurried, eyes on the lens. Storm wind lifts the sheer jungle-print chiffon and streams the long sleeves sideways; palms bend; lantern flames flicker and swing on their hooks; light rain slants; surf rolls in behind. Impressionist: the lantern glow smears into the wet dusk like warm copper oil paint, the storm sky shimmering like a freshly painted canvas. Camera dollies back slowly at her walking pace, one continuous take.
keep_still: Her face and his face exactly as in the frame; no talking, no lip movement. The man stays seated in profile holding the open jewellery box, and the necklace stays in the box. The plunging neckline stays closed and in place; nothing slips. No new people, no cuts.
risk: This shot has the most motion in my set. The 6 Oct s13 test (same frame, same move) held her face on Kling O3 4K. Watch for the neckline shifting in the wind and the slit opening too far, and reject any take where fabric slips. Text is 46 chars (3.5 s), so the 4 s minimum applies. A 5 s clip at 1.2 gives 6 s, which leaves room to trim.
note: Rendered on Kling O3 4K (the others are Kling O3 Pro).

motion: His fingers close the clasp at the back of her neck in one small precise movement, then lift slowly away and rest on her shoulders. She stays upright and still, eyes on the lens, only her breath moving under the necklace; the emeralds catch the lantern light. Rain falls in slow silver lines; lantern flames flicker; the lightning fades into a violet afterglow that pulses once across the wet tablecloth. Impressionist: rain-light runs over her skin like wet brushstrokes. Locked-off camera, then an almost imperceptible push-in on her face.
keep_still: Both faces unchanged, and his eyes stay lowered to the clasp. No speaking and no lip movement: both lines are silent text. She does not turn or lean. Dress, neckline and gold buckle stay in place. The necklace design stays unchanged. No kiss, no new people.
risk: The lightning bolt may stay as a static line or strike again; keep one flash and trim. The necklace may morph during the clasp action. His hands at her throat must read as fastening, never gripping. Two cards plus the voice come to 129 chars (9.9 s), so this needs a 10 s clip. One 4K take costs about $4.62.

motion: Near-still. The low sun sinks: peach light slowly deepens to copper across her cheek, and as it travels the fine craquelure at the corner of her eye catches it with a dry golden glint, like old varnish under a gallery lamp. Waves roll in slowly on the black sand behind; a warm breeze lifts a few loose strands of her hair and stirs his locs; the frangipani petals tremble. He keeps studying her like a canvas, gaze steady. Camera: very slow push-in toward her eye.
keep_still: Both faces unchanged. The cracks stay exactly where they are and do not spread or grow. Her head stays lowered and he stays seated. No talking, no lip movement. Nothing is added to the table and no new people appear. The three church bells are sound only; nothing visible shows them.
risk: As the light moves, the craquelure may spread across her face or vanish; reject either. Watch for drift in Jean-Marc's face and for her lifting her eyes. Text is 40 chars (3.1 s), but the edit is held to 5 s so the three bell strikes fit, as the Mila doc specifies.

motion: She finishes rising slowly and brushes her white silk dress once; a soft plume of ultramarine pigment drifts down from it and settles over the black sand around her bare feet, glowing faintly like coloured dust in the dusk. His outstretched hand closes slowly on empty air. The silk sways in the night breeze; small waves wash in; the first stars stay sharp; the candle on the sofa table flickers. Camera locked, a slight drift toward his closing hand.
keep_still: Her face and smile unchanged, and his face unchanged in profile. She does not walk out of frame, and his hand never reaches her wrist; it closes on air. The hem stays at the knee. No new people and nothing added in the pavilion or on the sofa behind.
risk: A 5 s clip at 1.2 gives exactly the 6 s needed, with no handles; use a 10 s clip if the action lands late. The pigment may turn into smoke or fire, or tint all the sand blue. The hem may lift too high. The extract also carries the source sentence; reading time counts only the on-screen clause (75 chars, 5.8 s).

motion: Only light moves. The candle flame flickers, and with each flicker the woman in the window breathes faintly in and out of transparency like a reflection, then settles. Beyond the glass the night sea moves in slow ultramarine ripples; the far lights on the water shimmer. The black curls in the foreground stir with one slow breath. Camera locked-off.
keep_still: The translucent woman stays seated on the ledge with her face and gaze unchanged, looking back. She never turns solid and never disappears. The sofa stays empty and the shoes stay where they are. The foreground woman does not turn, so her face is never seen. No new people.
risk: Kling may make the ghost solid or move her off the ledge. The foreground figure may turn and invent a face that is not in the approved frame. Only the on-screen clause counts toward reading time (94 chars, 7.2 s); the source context in the extract does not.

motion: They sit locked, staring at each other without blinking. The match burns steady and flickers at her open eye but never shortens. Crimson storm light pulses through the shutter slats and their bar-shadows slide slowly across faces, shoulders and hands: the body stays, the light moves. Rain beads run down the shutters; droplets glint on the cage bars. Only breath moves in their chests; his fingertips rest on her wrist. Camera locked-off, an imperceptible push-in.
keep_still: Faces unchanged: no blinking, no talking. No leaning in, no kiss, no new touch. The birdcage stays (her call) and neither it nor the armchairs move. Slip, strap and necklace stay in place. No new people or objects.
risk: Kling tends to blink, so pick the take with the fewest blinks. Reject any take where the match burns down or flares. Card plus voice need 12.6 s at 13 chars/s, but the cap is 10 s, so the voice has to run under the card. This is a never-cut shot.

motion: His fingers close the emerald clasp at the nape of her neck slowly, in one deliberate movement, then rest lightly on her skin. Her shoulders rise once with a slow breath; a water bead slides down her shoulder blade. The emeralds throw a faint green light that moves over her skin like light through sea water; above her shoulder the warm air trembles faintly, her perfume made visible as heat haze. The lamp behind flickers softly. Camera locked, slight push-in on the clasp.
keep_still: She never turns: back of the head and nape only, with no face visible. Framing stays at the shoulders and the camera never tilts down. Hair and necklace design unchanged. No new hands or people.
risk: The three cards come to 156 chars (12 s) but the cap is 10 s, so they need a tight split or one card trimmed; that is Elena's call. In close-up the clasp and links may morph, and the hands may grow extra fingers. The approved frame is a hands-and-nape macro, not the scenario's profile-plus-face framing.

motion: Hard white noon. Palm fronds sway in the trade wind and their black shadows shift on the sand; heat shimmer rises off the black sand so the air trembles like wet paint. Her curls lift a little in the wind; her dress hem stirs. She slowly lifts her eyes from the sand and looks across the empty beach to the right, then holds still. Camera locked-off, no movement at all (a figure is composited onto this plate in post).
keep_still: Her face unchanged, and she does not walk. Her own shadow stays at her feet. The beach stays empty and nothing enters the frame: no animals, no people. The rock and the mountains do not move.
risk: Kling may invent an animal or a person on the empty sand; reject the take, because the shadowless dog is a composite. Any camera drift ruins the keying plate. Strong heat shimmer will make the dog key harder. Text is 106 chars (8.2 s).

motion: Her fingertips glide slowly a few centimetres along one carved groove, feeling it. The raking sunbeam travels across the relief like slow honey, deepening and lifting the shadows inside the grooves as it moves. Dust motes drift through the beam; the curtains at the back breathe in a faint draft. Camera: slow push-in toward her fingertips.
keep_still: The carving stays abstract and unchanged: no figures, faces, letters or symbols emerge. The hands keep their shape, five fingers each. Room and armchair unchanged; no people appear.
risk: Reject any take where the relief morphs into figures or legible marks; also check the finger count. A 5 s clip at 1.2 gives exactly the 6 s needed, with no handles. This frame is also the mask source for shot 26, so the relief must stay identical.

motion: The forearm lies still. A cool blue-white light slides slowly along the inside of the arm from elbow to wrist, following the vein; the water beads glint as it passes; the fine hairs stir in a breath of air. The blue vein line shimmers faintly, like ink spreading in wet paper. A barely visible pulse at the wrist. Camera locked-off (code is composited along the vein in post).
keep_still: The arm does not move or rotate, and the skin texture stays unchanged. No writing, letters, tattoos or symbols appear on the skin. The vein line keeps its path. Nothing enters the frame.
risk: Kling may draw scribbles or text on the skin; reject, because the code is a composite. The vein shimmer must stay ink-blue so it never reads as a bruise or wound. Camera drift breaks tracking for the code. Text is 91 chars (7 s).

motion: She sits still in the third row, eyes on the lens, only her breath moving. Around her the raised white paddles drift slowly in the dark like a tide; on each, a soft crimson light spreads over the white face and fades, like red ink in snow. Wet hair and skin glint; the aisle lights flicker and their reflections tremble on the wet floor. Camera: slow push-in on her face.
keep_still: Her face unchanged; no talking. The bidders stay where they are with their faces unchanged. No new people or hands, and no numbers or text on the paddles. Ule is not in this frame.
risk: Faces in the crowd may morph, and the paddles may sprout numbers. The crimson must stay light, never liquid; 'blood' is deliberately not in the prompt because it is on the negative list. Timing assumes this shot carries the voice plus 'blood on snow' (121 chars, 9.3 s). 'the painting is the house itself.' goes on 20b, as the scenario says ('Text, on Ule').

motion: He keeps his palm flat on the wall, looking back over his shoulder, still. Leaf shadows sway slowly across the plaster; dust drifts through the sunbeam. Under his hand the stained plaster slowly warms with faint Gauguin colours (ochre, rose, deep green) blooming in the stains like a fresco surfacing, then sinking back. His linen shirt stirs with a slow breath. Camera: very slow push-in.
keep_still: His face, eyes and hair unchanged; he does not turn, walk or speak. His hand stays on the wall. The colour stays inside the stains, with no figures, faces or images painted on the wall. No people.
risk: Reject any take where the colour bloom becomes a recognisable painting or figures. His eye-line may drift. Text is 33 chars (2.5 s), so the 4 s minimum applies. The extract lists this line under shot 20; it belongs here.

motion: Her hand tilts the swollen black notebook slowly up into the shaft of light so the scratches on its cover catch it like an old scar, then draws it a little toward her, out of the light. Dust motes fall slowly through the beam; cobwebs sway; the light through the broken boards above flickers faintly, as if someone walks overhead. Camera: slow push-in on the cover.
keep_still: The notebook stays closed. The scratches stay random lines, and no letters or words form. One hand only, five fingers; no face or body appears. Nothing added.
risk: The notebook may open and invent handwriting; reject, because the line is burned-in text. 'Paradise.sol' must not be generated on the cover. Watch for hand drift or extra fingers. Text is 46 chars (3.5 s), so the 4 s minimum applies.

motion: Ule stands at the open night window, still, not turning; lips closed, no speech, no head turn. Only his chest breathes slowly. Fine rain falls beyond the palm fronds; one wet frond sways a little; the far lights on the black bay tremble and smear into soft impressionist strokes on the water. The oil-lamp flame flickers, its honey glow breathing on his shoulder and jaw. His reflection in the casement glass stays locked to him; raindrops trickle down the pane. Nobody enters. Camera locked-off, a barely perceptible push-in.
keep_still: Ule's face, profile and posture (no turn toward camera, no lip movement: 'No. Nothing.' is Kira's voice, added in post from off-frame); his forearm on the sill; the reflection in the glass (must not move on its own or become a second person); no new people.
risk: The reflection in the casement may animate on its own or turn toward the lens, so it reads as a second Ule. Reject those takes. Kling may also turn his head 'to answer'. The 5 s clip leaves no trim handle around the 4 s card plus the spoken lie. If the silence after 'No. Nothing.' needs to breathe, render 10 s. The extract's line for 22 carries a parse leftover ('Ничего.», #093)'). Only '— Found anything? —' goes on screen.

motion: Extreme close-up, Ule's wet face perfectly still, eyes open and glistening on the lens; mouth closed and unmoving, no sobbing, no frown change, no fluttering blinks. One new tear slowly wells and runs down the existing trail on his cheek; older trails dry to fine white salt. His chest rises once, slowly. The warm lamp bokeh behind him pulses gently like candle flame, and a faint cool shimmer, like light through melting ice, slides slowly across his cheekbone. Face shape and identity unchanged. Camera locked, no push.
keep_still: His whole face, eyes, gaze and mouth (no sobbing, no speech); head position; hair; the cord necklace; no second person.
risk: A 10 s frontal face close-up is where Kling drifts identity most. Compare the last frame with the keyframe (eyes, stubble, age). Tears can turn into white paint, glycerine streaks or blood. Reject any red. The reading load is the card (38 chars) plus the #043 voice draft (83 chars), about 9.3 s. If the 10 s take drifts, use the first 5 s and let the voice run under 25.

motion: Macro, no eyes, no mouth. Her fingertip travels very slowly along the thin white salt trail on his cheek, a few millimetres only, as if reading a map; his skin and stubble stay still. Sweat beads glint. The crimson lamp behind breathes softly; red light pulses over the skin like a slow heartbeat, its edge bleeding warm like watercolour. The salt stays a fine white line, never blood or a cut. No face turns into frame, no second hand appears, nothing added. Camera macro, locked, a slow slight push-in.
keep_still: His cheek, stubble and the framing (no eye, mouth or full face entering); the salt trail's shape and colour; the background room; one hand only. Do not add the scenario's shirt-falls-open beat, because no shirt is in this frame.
risk: The extract parser dropped 25's voice: the #042 draft is about 250 chars, about 19 s, and cannot fit in a 10 s shot. With the 77-char card, 25 is about 25 s of words for 10 s of picture. The voice must run under 24 to 26 or be shortened, and that is Elena's call. On macro skin Kling may morph the cheek, grow a nail or knuckle, or turn the salt line into a scratch. Reject red takes.

motion: Locked-off. Both faces stay still, gazes held on the lens, lips closed, no fluttering blinks, no head turns, no kiss. The carved moonlight lace from the window drifts very slowly across his face, chest and her fingers, as if clouds pass the moon, breathing brighter and dimmer like brushwork. Her palm rests flat on his chest; her fingertips move a millimetre, reading the light like braille. A steady pulse shows at his throat; his chest rises once. One wet curl of hers stirs. The moon shimmers. His shirt opens no further. Nothing added.
keep_still: Both faces and gazes (Kira behind his shoulder, Ule frontal), head positions, her hand's placement over his heart, the open shirt exactly as framed, the carved window and pendant; no third person.
risk: Over the cap: 3 cards (128 chars) plus the #021 voice (91 chars) is about 17 s for a 10 s maximum. Split a card onto 27 or let the voice run under the next shot. Two frontal faces for 10 s in 4K is the highest identity-drift case. Check both last-frame faces, and that Kira's hair stays black, not blue. The light pattern may slide off as a flat overlay or freeze. The carved light should move over the skin, not on top of it.

motion: Macro, no face. The man's fingertip glides very slowly down along the pale hairline scar, a short way only, barely pressing. Her back stays still except one slow breath lifting the shoulder blades. The single black curl stirs; one water bead slides slowly down the skin. Soft honey side-light travels slowly across her back, the shadow between the shoulder blades softening like wet paint. The scar stays faint, pale, healed, skin-toned: never red, raw, bleeding or a wound. No second hand, no turning, nothing added. Camera locked, macro.
keep_still: Her back, posture and the framing (no face, no turn, nothing below the shoulder blades revealed); the scar's colour and width; one fingertip only.
risk: Text is 159 chars, about 12 s, so it is about 2 s over the 10 s cap. Tighten or split the four cards. Kling has turned this scar into a red wound before (film #8). Reject any take where it reddens or opens. The keyframe has baked letterbox bars top and bottom; crop at compile and make sure Kling does not animate them. The finger may sprout a second hand or extra joints.

motion: Macro, near-still. His lips move only faintly under her two fingers, as if forming words that never sound: mouth stays almost closed, no opening, no teeth, no kissing or taking her fingers. Her fingers rest lightly and stay where they are. One slow breath through his nose; his chest rises once. Behind, faint smoke drifts, the two lamps flicker, the red jungle flowers barely stir; the crimson light on her fingers pulses softly, as if with his unspoken words. No eyes enter frame, nothing added. Camera locked.
keep_still: Her two fingers' position on his lips; his face from nose to chin (no eyes entering frame); the shirt; the empty background, with no figures in the seats.
risk: Over the cap: 5 cards (210 chars) is about 16 s for 10 s. Split across shots or trim cards; that is Elena's call.
